items.actClause: AN ACT to amend chapter 589 of the laws of 2015 amending the insurance law relating to catastrophic or reinsurance coverage issued to certain small groups, in relation to the effectiveness thereof; to amend chapter 588 of the laws of 2015 amending the insurance law relating to catastrophic or reinsurance coverage issued to certain small groups, in relation to the effectiveness thereof; and in relation to directing the superintendent of financial services to add certain other health insurance matters to the assessment study of the impact of the prohibition on the sale of stop loss, catastrophic and reinsurance coverage to the small group market

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6572

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend chapter 589 of the laws of 2015
amending the insurance law relating to catastrophic or reinsurance
coverage issued to certain small groups, in relation to the
effectiveness thereof; to amend chapter 588 of the laws of 2015
amending the insurance law relating to catastrophic or reinsurance
coverage issued to certain small groups, in relation to the
effectiveness thereof; and in relation to directing the superintendent
of financial services to add certain other health insurance matters to
the assessment study of the impact of the prohibition on the sale of
stop loss, catastrophic and reinsurance coverage to the small group
market

 PURPOSE :

The purpose of this bill is to allow stop loss, catastrophic and
reinsurance coverages to remain in effect for certain self-funded
small groups for one additional year.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Sections 1 and 2 of the bill would allow for the continuation for an
additional year of the sale of stop loss, catastrophic or reinsurance
coverages, which were in effect on January 1, 2015, despite a general
prohibition which would prevent insurers from selling this kind of
coverage to groups with 51-100 employees, members or subscribers as of
January 1, 2016.

Section 3 of the bill would add certain additional health insurance
matters to be included for general review in the assessment study
being conducted by a consultant to the department of financial
services (DFS) pursuant to the provisions of section 7 of chapter 12
of the laws of 2016.

Section 4 of the bill sets forth the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The federal Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (ACA) expanded
the "small group" market up to 100 employees, members or subscribers
effective January 1, 2016, to which New York conformed its laws.
Expanding the size of small group up to 100 employees, members or
subscribers in New York required the sale of community-rated policies
and prohibited the sale of stop loss, reinsurance or catastrophic
coverages to mid-sized groups with 51-100 employees, members or
subscribers for the first time. This included both private sector
firms, labor union groups, municipal cooperatives and school and
library district consortiums.

This bill would extend for one additional year until December 31,
2019, the grandfathering of mid-sized groups with 51-100 employees,
members or subscribers that currently self-fund with stop loss
coverage, as long as they keep their coverage in effect. This will
allow such groups additional time to transition into the small group
market while awaiting the DFS assessment study. The bill also adds
certain additional matters to be reviewed as part of the ongoing stop
loss insurance assessment study in order to measure the impact of such
matters upon the availability, affordability and quality of coverage
in the small group market.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6572A

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend chapter 589 of the laws of 2015,
amending the insurance law relating to catastrophic or reinsurance
coverage issued to certain small groups, in relation to the
effectiveness thereof; and to amend chapter 588 of the laws of 2015,
amending the insurance law relating to catastrophic or reinsurance
coverage issued to certain small groups, in relation to the
effectiveness thereof

 PURPOSE :

The purpose of this bill is to allow stop loss, catastrophic and
reinsurance coverages to remain in effect for certain self-funded
small groups for one additional year.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of the bill would extend for an additional year the
provisions of chapter 589 of the laws of 2015, as amended by chapter
12 of the laws of 2016, which provided that small groups between the
size of 51-100 who had reinsurance policies in effect on 1/1/2015 may
continue to eligible to renew such policy or purchase re-insurance
between 1/1/2016 and 1/1/2017 and renew such policy thereafter, and
which also exempted municipal corporations with member employers with
100 or fewer employees from small group rating standards.

Section two of the bill would extend for an additional year the
provisions of chapter 588 of the laws of 2015, as amended by chapter
12 of the laws of 2016, which provided that small groups between the
size of 51-100 who had reinsurance policies in effect on 1/1/2015 may
continue to eligible to renew such policy or purchase re-insurance
between 1/1/2016 and 1/1/2017 and renew such policy thereafter, and
which also exempted municipal corporations with member employers with
100 or fewer employees from small group rating standards.

Section 3 of the bill sets forth the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The federal Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (ACA) expanded
the "small group" market up to 100 employees, members or subscribers
effective January 1, 2016, to which New York conformed its laws.
Expanding the size of small group up to 100 employees, members or
subscribers in New York required the sale of community-rated policies
and prohibited the sale of stop loss, reinsurance or catastrophic
coverages to midsized groups with 51-100 employees, members or
subscribers for the first time. This included both private sector
firms, labor union groups, municipal cooperatives and school and
library district consortiums.

This bill would extend for one additional year until December 31,
2019, the grandfathering of mid-sized groups with 51-100 employees,
members or subscribers that currently self-fund with stop loss
coverage, as long as they keep their coverage in effect. This will
allow such groups additional time to transition into the small group
market while awaiting the DFS assessment study.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately.
